intro: Tuple immutable sequence hai: banne ke baad uske items badal nahi sakte. Yahi property usse safe return values, dictionary keys aur fixed records ke liye perfect banati hai. Is section me tuple banane, unpack karne aur namedtuple tak ka safar hai.
theory: Tuple parentheses se banta hai, par asli comma constructor hai: `(5)` sirf int hai, `(5,)` ek-element tuple hai.
Immutability ka matlab hai ki item rebind nahi ho sakta; lekin tuple ke andar mutable object (jaise list) rakha ja sakta hai aur wo badal sakta hai.
Unpacking tuple ki sabse badi power hai: `a, b = b, a` swap, `first, *rest = data` split, aur function se multiple values return karna.
Tuple hashable hota hai jab uske saare items hashable hon — isliye tuple dict key ya set member ban sakta hai, list nahi.
namedtuple field names ke saath readable record deta hai aur phir bhi tuple ki unpacking aur immutability rakhta hai.
syntax:
point = (3, 4)
single = (5,)          # comma zaroori
empty = ()
from_list = tuple([1, 2, 2])

a, b = (1, 2)          # unpack
first, *rest = (1, 2, 3)
x, y = y, x            # swap
name, score = record   # record se values

point[0], point[-1]    # index
point[1:]              # slice -> naya tuple
tuple.count(x), tuple.index(x)
from collections import namedtuple

explain: count occurrences ginta hai aur index pehla position deta hai.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye Tuples ka basic building block hai.
Slicing tuple par naya tuple deti hai, original waisa hi rehta hai.
Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.

examples.code:
from collections import namedtuple

Reading = namedtuple('Reading', 'sensor value')
readings = [Reading('temp', 21.5), Reading('temp', 22.0), Reading('humidity', 45)]

for reading in readings:
    sensor, value = reading
    print(f'{sensor:<9} {value:>6}')

temps = [r.value for r in readings if r.sensor == 'temp']
print('avg temp:', sum(temps) / len(temps))
explain: namedtuple ko unpack karke aur attribute se padhkar grouped summary banayi ja sakti hai.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Coordinates, RGB colours aur (latitude, longitude) jaise fixed records tuple me rakhe jate hain — galti se badalne ka dar nahi rehta.
Function se `(value, error)` ya `(rows, skipped)` return karna tuple ka standard pattern hai; caller unpack karke dono handle karta hai.
Dictionary keys ke liye composite key `(user_id, date)` tuple banai jati hai; list se ye possible nahi hota.

interview.q: Tuple list se kaise alag hai, aur kab tuple chunenge?
interview.a: Tuple immutable aur hashable (agar items hashable hon) hota hai, list mutable. Fixed record, function return value aur dict key ke liye tuple; badalne wale collection ke liye list.

interview.q: Ek element ka tuple kaise banate hain?
interview.a: Trailing comma se: `(5,)`. `(5)` sirf int hai kyunki parentheses grouping karte hain, tuple comma banata hai.

interview.q: Kya tuple ke andar list rakh sakte hain?
interview.a: Haan, par tab tuple hashable nahi rahega aur andar ki list mutate ho sakti hai. Immutability sirf top-level bindings par lagti hai.

interview.q: namedtuple aur dataclass me kya choose karoge?
interview.a: namedtuple immutable, tuple-compatible aur sasta hai — fixed record ke liye. dataclass mutable ya frozen ho sakta hai, defaults/validation ke saath zyada readable hai, par tuple unpack nahi hota.

debugging.error: IndexError: list index out of range
debugging.why: List me sirf 0 aur 1 index hain; 5 par kuch nahi. Ye Tuples ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Index se pehle length check karo ya safe getter use karo.
debugging.correct:
scores = [10, 20]
print(scores[1] if len(scores) > 1 else None)
debugging.lesson: IndexError off-by-one aur empty collection ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye Tuples ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.

debugging.error: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'
debugging.why: int() sirf poore number ka string parse karta hai. Ye Tuples ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Pehle float() phir int() karo, ya Decimal use karo.
debugging.lesson: ValueError format ka issue hai, type ka nahi.

debugging.why: String immutable hai; append list ka method hai. Ye Tuples ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: String concatenation ya join use karo.
debugging.lesson: AttributeError galat type par method call ka signal hai.

revision: Tuples: revise create — Parentheses ke andar comma-separated values tuple banati hain.
Tuples: revise single_item — Ek item ka tuple banane ke liye trailing comma zaroori hai.
Tuples: revise unpack — Unpacking tuple ke items ko alag names par bind karti hai.
Tuples: revise star_unpack — Star-unpacking beech ke items ki list banati hai.
Tuples: revise swap — Right side pehle tuple ki tarah evaluate hoti hai, isliye swap bina temp ke hota hai.
